factProposals.value: A diagnosis is a required label (1 to 200 characters, one line) with an optional tooth (stored as its FDI key), optional notes (up to 1,000 characters) and an optional treatment-plan reference, recorded for one patient in one of that patient's encounters. Status is Active or Withdrawn; every record, correction and withdrawal appends a full snapshot to an append-only history.

The treatment-plan link is an optional opaque forward reference (trimmed, whitespace collapsed, up to 100 characters, never blank). It is not a foreign key, is never looked up, and is reported as 'Unresolved' whenever present. No treatment-plan table, API or record exists.

Anyone who may read clinical documentation (dentist, hygienist, assistant, admin) can see diagnoses and their history; roles that manage clinical notes (dentist, hygienist, admin) can record, correct and withdraw. The assistant reads but is refused (403) on writes; front desk and billing cannot see the tab and are refused (403); anonymous callers get 401 and writes without a CSRF token are refused.

The Diagnoses tab of the patient workspace lists a patient's diagnoses newest first with the encounter, tooth, notes, who recorded each and when, and the treatment-plan reference labelled unresolved with a statement that it does not mean a plan exists. Each diagnosis opens to its history. An empty list says none has been recorded, and a failed load says so.

Incorrect diagnosis data is refused with every problem listed (field, stable code, message) and nothing saved: missing or other-patient encounter, blank or control-character or over-long label, unknown tooth, over-long notes, blank or over-long reference, a missing correction reason, replacing and clearing the reference together. The screen checks the same rules first, links each problem to its box and keeps what was typed; the database repeats the checks.

Every record, correction and withdrawal is written to the audit log with the signed-in user and a timestamp in the same save as the diagnosis and its history version, so a failed log write stores nothing and the person is told. Audit text carries no label, tooth, notes or reference.

A diagnosis can never be deleted (trigger 51071), its history is append-only (51072), its patient, encounter and origin never change (51073) and its encounter must belong to its patient (51074). Recording is idempotent per patient by key; the same key with a different entry is refused with 409.

decisions.statement: The treatment-plan link is stored as an optional typed forward reference and not as a plan record or foreign key.
decisions.rationale: Treatment plans do not exist yet and their domain belongs to ALV-015-C01; the reference satisfies the linkage requirement without claiming a plan exists, and can be reconciled later.

decisions.statement: The reference changes only by an explicit, recorded act: a correction that omits it keeps it, a value replaces it, and a separate clear flag removes it; every value stays in the history with the reason.
decisions.rationale: A correction that merely left the field out must never silently drop or replace a link.

decisions.statement: A diagnosis is never deleted; a wrong one is corrected or withdrawn with a reason and stays in the record.
decisions.rationale: The trust criterion requires every entry to be logged with user and time; deleting would erase clinical history.

decisions.statement: Diagnoses may be recorded against finalized encounters, and an encounter of another patient is refused identically to a missing one.
decisions.rationale: A diagnosis is its own record with its own history and does not alter the encounter notes; identical refusals avoid revealing other patients' encounters.

decisions.statement: Reading and writing reuse the existing clinical-documentation permissions; no role matrix changed.
decisions.rationale: Diagnoses are clinical documentation and the existing boundary already matches the story's actors.

limitations.statement: No coding system: a diagnosis is a free-text label; codes, provenance and a structured lifecycle are left to ALV-013-C01.
The treatment-plan reference is never resolved or validated against a plan; reconciliation is left to ALV-015-C01.
Status is Active or Withdrawn only, one tooth per diagnosis, and a diagnosis cannot be moved to another encounter.
A diagnosis needs an existing encounter; none can be started from the Diagnoses screen.
Hygienists can record diagnoses because they hold the clinical-notes permission.
